title: Seller-Brain Capture and Margin Leak Audit
one_liner: In the 90-day handover, reverse-engineer the retiring owner's pricing and rules of thumb from years of quotes and invoices, and find the contract and price leaks the seller never fixed, for a fee tied to recovered margin.
customer: First-time acquirers (search funders, independent sponsors, SBA-financed buyers, small holdcos) of $1-15M revenue service and light-manufacturing firms. SBA lenders and brokers are secondary referrers.
problem: The seller's pricing logic lives in his head, records are paper or Excel, and the handover is a 'handshake and good luck'. New owners find contractual minimums unbilled, price books frozen for years, parts sold below cost, and waste in telecom and software. They discover this only after closing, when the seller is already leaving.
solution: A 30-day sprint at signing or close. (1) Ingest 3 years of quotes, invoices, price books, contracts and vendor, phone and SaaS bills, including scanned paper. (2) An AI model reconstructs the implicit pricing rules and flags exceptions. (3) A structured, recorded 3-hour seller interview validates and labels the rules. (4) Output a working quote calculator, a written 'rules of thumb' manual, and a ranked leak list in dollars (unbilled contractual minimums, stale prices vs inflation, below-cost jobs and parts, dead subscriptions). The seller reviews the model weekly during the transition period.
why_now: Bain's 2026 reports say deals now need 10-12% EBITDA growth to hit returns and 79% of GPs expect flat purchase multiples, so operational upside has to be found rather than bought. Buyers of small firms feel the same pressure. LLMs now read messy PDFs, scans and Excel cheaply, which makes a 10-day audit cost a few hundred dollars in compute instead of a consultant's month.
revenue_model: $4-6K fixed fee for the capture sprint, plus 10-15% of annualized recovered margin in year one (capped). Optional pre-LOI 'upside memo' at $1.5-2.5K that buyers use to justify a bid and negotiate price.
non_obvious_insight: The leaks are contractual and forgotten, not strategic, and the seller's pricing logic is a perishable asset that expires with the transition period. Concrete cases from ETA operators: Tew & Taylor's contracts specified a two-hour minimum but the prior owner billed one hour, and after the buyer applied the contract rate there was 'virtually no customer pushback' (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/jack-rauch-tew-taylor). At Cardinal Heating & Air, prices were unchanged since pre-COVID, parts were sold below cost, and the buyer cut $1.4M of annualized cost in two weeks ($10K/month in cell phones vs $3K needed). Gross margins went from 7-20% to 48-49% (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/mike-bourgeois-cardinal-heating-and-air). At Winsor Fireform, pricing was the seller's 27 years of 'hunches', and the buyers 'sprinted' to extract it into a model during his 3-month transition; gross margin rose from 55% to 58-59% (https://acquiringminds.co/articles/andrew-sova-alex-clark-winsor-fireform-novo-foundry). At Gary Air, prices had not kept pace with inflation for 4+ years, and earnings went from $340K SDE to $1.3M EBITDA in 14 months (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/rob-brooks-gary-air). Four independent buyers found the same class of leak and each rebuilt it by hand.
first_30_days: Offer free audits to 10 first-time buyers found in ETA communities (Searchfunder, Acquiring Minds audience, ETA subreddits) in exchange for permission to publish anonymized before/after numbers. Build parsers for QuickBooks exports and for invoice exports from ServiceTitan, Jobber and Housecall Pro, plus a vendor-bill classifier. Create a one-page seller-interview protocol. Convert the first 3 free audits into case studies, then switch to contingency pricing.

title: Notary-Witnessed Hiring Against Deepfake Candidates
one_liner: On-demand licensed notaries sit beside a remote candidate for the final interview or day-one onboarding and sign an attestation.
customer: Security and talent leads at remote-first software, fintech and defence-contractor employers, plus technical recruiting agencies, staffing firms and employer-of-record providers.
problem: An August 2026 eleven-nation advisory warned that North Korean IT-worker operations use real-time deepfakes to beat hiring checks, with 6,500+ similar cases reported globally. Employers face sanctions exposure. Liveness and document checks are being defeated, and the only alternatives are flying candidates in or trusting software.
solution: A marketplace and quality layer over existing mobile notaries and I-9 authorised representatives. A candidate books a witnessed final round in their own city. The witness checks ID, sweeps the room and desk for second screens and earpieces, positions a second camera, and signs a sealed attestation. An optional witnessed live-coding session runs on a locked, company-supplied laptop. A second 10-minute witnessed check at day 30 confirms identity continuity. Coverage starts in 200 US metros and expands to the UK and EU.
why_now: Real-time deepfake interviews are now mainstream and the 11-nation advisory (Aug 2026) is prompting boards to act. The DHS remote I-9 alternative procedure already blesses human 'authorised representatives'. Mobile signing agents lost volume when mortgage origination slumped, so witness supply is cheap.
revenue_model: $150-350 per witnessed session (about 60% to the witness), $2-10k per month enterprise subscriptions, and a per-hire fee for staffing agencies.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders think software has to beat deepfakes. For high-stakes moments, the cheapest defence is physics. A $200 human in the room costs less than one failed hire, and the scarce input is legally recognised people who already verify identity for a living. There are millions of commissioned US notaries.
first_30_days: Sign 40 notaries and loan-signing agents in five metros through signing-agent communities. Write a witness protocol and kit checklist, with legal review of what a notary may attest outside a notarial act. Pilot with three staffing firms or security-conscious startups.

title: Test-once PFAS proof registry for packaging importers
one_liner: A SKU-level registry and group-buy of accredited PFAS lab reports, so importers of the same factory's food packaging share one test and can produce an authority-ready dossier fast.
customer: EU importers, wholesalers and white-label brands of grease-resistant paper and fibre food packaging (takeaway boxes, bakery bags, burger wraps, pizza boxes, cups), plus online B2B packaging shops. Owners, purchasing or QA managers pay.
problem: Since 12 Aug 2026 the packaging regulation bans PFAS in food-contact packaging above limits (25 ppb per non-polymeric substance, 250 ppb sum, 50 ppm total PFAS), with no grandfathering for stock made earlier. Compliance guides say supplier self-declarations are not proof and that importers and producers carry the liability, with accredited-lab reports needed per packaging type. Authorities can request the technical documentation on short notice. There is no harmonised EU test method and lab capacity is finite. Each importer paying separately for the same factory's product is wasteful.
solution: A registry keyed to product specification, coating, factory and production lot. Factories, labs and importers upload accredited lab reports (cheap total organic fluorine screening first, then targeted LC-MS/MS). Other importers of the same factory and spec can match and attach the report to their own technical file. A lot-matching check and re-test reminders keep the proof valid, and an 'authority request pack' export assembles the file in one click. Group-buy: when several importers sell the same SKU, the platform pools the cost of one accredited test and negotiates volume prices with 2-3 labs. Each importer remains legally responsible, so the tool shows exactly what evidence it does and does not cover.
why_now: The ban applied on 12 Aug 2026, six weeks ago, and stock made before then cannot be sold. Labs expect demand to climb through enforcement and there is no harmonised method yet, so evidence quality varies.
revenue_model: EUR 150-400 per verified report access, EUR 25 per month per SKU for monitoring and re-test alerts, plus a 10-15% margin on group-purchased lab tests. Optional paid dossier assembly at EUR 300-600.
non_obvious_insight: Every importer treats PFAS proof as its own cost, but the object being proven is the packaging type. The same few hundred factory SKUs flow through thousands of importers, which creates network effects for a 'test once, verify per lot' registry that no consultancy or lab has an incentive to build. Evidence: guides state that 'self-declarations from suppliers do not constitute proof' and that certificates of analysis are needed per packaging type (https://www.certivo.com/blog-details/ppwr-pfas-ban-in-food-contact-packaging-what-manufacturers-must-have-ready-by-august-2026); the ban has no grandfather clause and responsibility falls on manufacturers and importers (https://www.kivo.nl/en/knowledge-base/pfas-ban-in-food-packaging-what-does-it-mean-for-your-products/); testing runs from a few hundred euros for screening to several thousand for targeted analysis, labs have limited capacity, and no harmonised EU method exists (https://pakfactory.com/blog/how-to-test-packaging-for-pfas; https://foodpackagingforum.org/news/ppwr-pfas-limits-apply-from-august-12).
first_30_days: Sign volume pricing with 2 accredited labs for TOF screening and targeted panels. Recruit 10 importers from packaging trade associations, LinkedIn groups and B2B packaging marketplaces. Ask them to list their top 20 SKUs and factories, then find overlaps between them. Run the first pooled test for the most-shared SKU at a per-importer cost far below a solo test. Publish a free 'PFAS status per SKU' lookup to attract more importers. Legal-review the shared-report disclaimer language with a food-contact lawyer.

title: Vet-Prescribed Walks for Post-Surgery and Senior Dogs
one_liner: Certify dog walkers to deliver vet-written controlled-walking protocols after cruciate and spinal surgery, and to send structured mobility reports back to the clinic.
customer: Owners of dogs recovering from orthopedic or spinal surgery (TPLO, luxating patella, IVDD) and owners of senior arthritic dogs. Referral partners are surgical and rehab vet practices, who get reports at no charge.
problem: Discharge sheets say things like '5-minute leash walks four times a day, add 5 minutes a week,' and working owners cannot do it. Dogs get over-exercised or under-exercised and some re-tear the repair, which is a $4k to $6k mistake. Most walkers are afraid of the liability, and most vets don't trust an unspecified walker to follow a protocol. Meanwhile arthritic seniors decline slowly and owners miss it, while the walker sees the hesitation at stairs and the shorter walks first.
solution: A short walker certification (protocol cards written with two partner rehab vets, sling and non-slip handling, escalation rules). Visits are timed, leash-controlled, and followed by a structured report covering minutes walked, a 0 to 4 gait score, stiffness on rising, toileting, and a 15-second weight-bearing video. The report goes to the owner and the clinic ahead of the 2, 6, and 8 week rechecks. Red flags (swelling, heat, toe-touching) trigger a same-day call. A senior SKU gives a monthly mobility check with a gait video and pain questionnaire, so owner and vet can see whether joint meds or the newer arthritis injectables are actually working.
why_now: Vets are short-staffed and cannot run rehab follow-ups themselves. Pet insurance adoption keeps growing, so owners protecting a multi-thousand-dollar surgery will pay for compliance. The newer arthritis injectables raised the need for objective at-home response tracking, and safety debates around them make vets want data. Return-to-office pushes more owners out of the house all day right when recoveries need multiple short visits.
revenue_model: Post-op bundle of roughly $900 to $1,800 over 6 to 8 weeks (short visits at $30 to $45), with the walker keeping about 70 percent. Walker certification fee of roughly $250 to $300. Senior monitoring subscription at about $39 a month. No referral kickbacks to vets, so it stays clean; clinics get the free reports and fewer failed recoveries.
non_obvious_insight: The most valuable clients in this business are not the healthy dogs on the schedule, they are post-op and declining dogs, because the protocol needs several short, geographically tight visits a day and the owner is desperate. The gap is trust, not supply: a protocol and a report format turn 'a walker' into a rehab extender that vets will refer to.
first_30_days: Sit down with the techs at two local surgical or rehab practices and write a one-page walking progression with them. Get yourself and three walkers through a dry run. Offer the first 10 post-op dogs a reduced bundle in exchange for report feedback, using a simple form that generates a PDF. Ask each clinic to slip a card into TPLO discharge packets and track how many convert.

title: Apprentice Athlete: Injury-Proofing the Skilled Trades
one_liner: An 8-week pre-apprenticeship that conditions and movement-screens new electricians, plumbers and pipefitters so they survive the first two years.
customer: Joint apprenticeship training centers (IBEW/NECA, UA, IEC, ABC), community-college trade programs, and the workers' comp carriers and brokers behind contractors. Contractors pay per placed apprentice.
problem: Electricians have about 72.7k openings a year (data-center demand) and plumbers about 42k, but the 4-5 year apprenticeship path is bottlenecked by employer sponsors and weak pre-apprenticeship screening. Overexertion and strain injuries are consistently a leading cause of lost-time injuries and feed early attrition. Many entrants are sedentary career-changers, including displaced white-collar grads (42% of recent grads are underemployed).
solution: 'Apprentice Athlete' runs 3 sessions a week for 8 weeks in existing gyms, taught by athletic trainers and strength coaches. It uses trade-specific drills (overhead conduit work, ladder and pipe carries, crawlspace mobility, grip endurance), phone-video or cheap-wearable movement screens, and an injury-prevention curriculum. Completion, not a fitness score, earns JATC pre-apprenticeship credit and can slot in as a short program eligible for Workforce Pell where approved. It is structured as training rather than a hiring screen, to stay clear of ADA limits.
why_now: Workforce Pell launched July 1, 2026 but only 5 programs are approved. Apprenticeship-linked programs get a fast lane, and up to 49% of instruction can be delivered by employers or unions. Data-center demand is pulling electricians, and AI-exposed grads are pivoting to trades. Phone pose-estimation and cheap wearables are now good enough to measure movement quality.
revenue_model: $400-800 per apprentice per cohort paid by contractor, JATC or Pell/WIOA funds. A $100-200k pilot contract with a comp carrier tied to premium credits. Then per-seat licensing to gyms and trainers who run the program (they keep 60-70%).
non_obvious_insight: The trades treat the body as a consumable, while sports treat it as an appreciating asset. Comp carriers already have loss runs showing injuries cluster in the first 24 months, so a $600 conditioning program pays back if it prevents one strain claim per few dozen apprentices. Trade schools cannot have that ROI conversation, but insurers can.
first_30_days: Partner with one IEC/ABC chapter or a community-college trades program. Run a 6-week pilot for 20 career-changers using phone-video screening and a $50 tracker. Log attendance, attrition and minor injuries against the prior cohort. Take the numbers to the contractors' workers' comp broker to negotiate a premium-credit pilot.

title: Integrity Desk for Grant Applications
one_liner: Cross-funder screening that catches AI-mass-produced applications, recycled proposals and forged partner letters before reviewers waste time.
customer: Community foundations, corporate giving programmes, state and regional economic-development agencies and accelerators, reached through grant-management platforms such as Submittable and Foundant.
problem: NIH capped principal investigators at six applications a year (effective 25 Sep 2025) after one applicant filed 40+ apparently AI-generated applications, and it says AI-developed proposals are not original work. Funders elsewhere see multiples of prior volume. Letters of support and partner commitments are the easiest thing to fabricate, and the same proposal is shopped to many funders.
solution: A plug-in and API for grant portals. It scores text reuse and AI boilerplate across applicants (including anonymised cross-funder fingerprints) and verifies claims and citations. It automatically calls back signatories of support letters for signed confirmation, checks entity registrations, tax status and beneficial owners, and keeps a shared duplicate-application registry across member funders.
why_now: LLMs drove the volume flood that prompted NIH's 2025 policy. Foundation staffing is thin, and federal and state scrutiny of grant fraud is rising.
revenue_model: $5-25k per cycle for foundations, $0.50-5 per application via portal partners, and registry membership for funders.
non_obvious_insight: This is the cURL lesson. When the cost of submission falls to zero, the reviewer's attention is the scarce resource. The winning move is not detecting AI text, which is unreliable, but verifying checkable third-party facts, like a partner's confirmation call, that AI cannot fake for free.
first_30_days: Run free pilot scans on last cycle's applications for three community foundations through regional grantmaker associations. Publish anonymised findings such as the share of applications with heavy text overlap. Pitch one grant-software vendor for a plug-in partnership.

title: Rescue Monitoring for Orphaned Home Solar
one_liner: An installer-agnostic gateway plus subscription that watches home solar systems whose installer went bankrupt, produces warranty-ready evidence, and dispatches a vetted local electrician.
customer: Homeowners with installer-abandoned solar systems (owned or financed). B2B: solar loan servicers and asset managers holding loans and leases from failed installers, who care about collateral performance. Local electricians and solar technicians are the fulfillment network.
problem: Installers such as Sunnova (Chapter 11 in June 2025, roughly 500,000 customers) and others collapsed. Systems keep running, but nobody is watching or servicing them. Silent faults (failed optimizers, tripped rapid shutdown, inverter errors) can cost months of production. Warranty claims require documentation the homeowner doesn't have, and installer apps degrade or vanish.
solution: A gateway that reads inverter data locally (SunSpec Modbus and local APIs) plus a CT clamp on the main panel. It compares actual output to modeled output using open weather and irradiance data, classifies probable fault types (string, inverter, shading, curtailment), and generates a warranty evidence pack for the equipment manufacturers. A flat-fee price sheet dispatches vetted local technicians. Start with the three or four most common inverter families.
why_now: The installer failure wave (SunPower in 2024, Sunnova in 2025, many smaller firms) is producing large orphaned fleets. The federal residential solar tax credit ended for expenditures after 2025, so more installers will exit and fewer new ones will absorb the orphans. Gateways and cloud analytics are now cheap.
revenue_model: USD 8-12 per month plus a USD 150-250 gateway or a USD 199 'solar health check plus 12 months' bundle. Dispatch margin of 15-20% on repairs. B2B data-and-triage feed of USD 2-4 per system per month for servicers with 10k+ systems.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing isn't data, because the inverter clouds still exist. It's someone accountable who reads the data and moves a truck. Sell a primary-care doctor for a solar system with a referral network. Lenders care because a non-producing system correlates with default, which gives a second payer.
first_30_days: Recruit orphan-solar homeowners through r/solar and Facebook groups. Ship 50 gateways to owners of two or three inverter families. Sign 3-5 electricians in Texas, California, Arizona or Florida on a fixed price sheet. Sell the health-check bundle and use the first detected faults as marketing proof. Approach two loan servicers with the aggregate underperformance findings.

title: One-Filing Shield for At-Risk Public Servants
one_liner: A single intake that files every county office's address-confidentiality forms, fixes what gets recorded next, and monitors leaks for judges, election officials and clinicians.
customer: County and municipal risk pools and insurers, state associations of election officials, clerks, judges and school boards, hospital systems and physician groups (employer benefit), and police unions. Paid per protected person per year.
problem: A determined stalker can find almost anyone's home address in 30 seconds through deeds, the assessor roll, the voter file, court files, marriage licenses and business filings. Confidentiality and redaction laws now exist in 30+ states, but each office (recorder, assessor, treasurer, court clerk, voter registration, business filings) has its own form and process, and none talk to each other. Redaction usually masks the online index while the image stays retrievable at the counter and in bulk data purchases, so people-search brokers re-scrape it. Broker-removal services only hit the last layer. Clerks are ministerial and legally barred from advising anyone, so nobody explains the fix.
solution: A concierge plus software product. One intake produces and files every state- and county-specific confidentiality request across all relevant offices, with notary and wet-ink logistics handled. A local attorney network handles retitling into a privacy land trust or LLC with agent-signed deeds and mailing-address-only recording before anything new is recorded. It moves the voter registration to protected status, scrubs business filings, monitors new recordings and assessor changes monthly for the client's name, and runs broker takedowns as a final layer. Publish a free county-by-county confidentiality forms map as the top-of-funnel.
why_now: The June 2025 Minnesota lawmaker shootings, in which the suspect allegedly used people-search sites to compile officials' addresses, pushed a wave of new laws. California AB 302 requires deletions within five days from August 1, 2026, and Delaware, Florida and Georgia have judge-protection statutes. Threats against election officials and the November 3, 2026 midterms keep the issue hot, and insurers are pushing risk mitigation onto pools and employers.
revenue_model: $180-$450 per protected person per year as a benefit purchased by pools, associations or employers, plus a one-time onboarding fee and attorney-fulfilled trust-deed packages at cost plus margin. Group pricing for a pool covering hundreds of officials.
non_obvious_insight: Redaction in a county system is a display mask, not deletion, so the leak returns through the image and bulk data. The real protection is changing what gets recorded before it is recorded, which is precisely what a clerk cannot tell anyone. The 'first mile' data source is the county, not the broker, and nobody in the privacy-service industry works the six separate county offices.
first_30_days: Pick one state with a friendly clerks' association and do concierge onboarding at cost for about 20 county clerks and election officials through that association. Publish the county-by-county forms map to earn trust and backlinks. Pitch one county risk pool a 100-person pilot at $250 per person, line up one local attorney for the trust-deed workflow, and collect testimonials from the first cohort.

title: Rural Jail Pharmacy-in-a-Box for Independents
one_liner: Turn the local independent's blister packing, delivery and controlled-substance discipline into a per-inmate contract for the county jail that the sheriff is afraid of.
customer: Sheriffs, jail administrators and county commissions running jails of about 20-150 beds, whose risk pools and insurers care about medication liability. Independent pharmacies are a second customer, licensing the playbook and software.
problem: Jail medication is a sheriff's biggest lawsuit exposure: missed doses, withdrawal, wrong-inmate errors, controlled-substance counts. Small jails run it with a deputy, a clipboard and a nurse who visits two days a week. Mail-order jail pharmacies take 3-5 days, so first-night meds come from the ER or a deputy's personal trip to the drugstore. Buprenorphine and other opioid-treatment mandates funded by opioid settlements add complexity. Meanwhile local independents already run the identical workflow for nursing homes.
solution: A repeatable program with same-day intake verification (call the outside pharmacy, check the PDMP). Barcode blister-packed med pass with an offline-capable eMAR on a tablet. Controlled-substance counts with dual sign-off and photo audit. An emergency kit and a monthly consultant-pharmacist review. A 30-day bridge supply at release. Sold as a playbook, software and group-purchasing bundle so any independent can become the county's jail pharmacy, with master agreements through state association-of-counties risk pools.
why_now: Wellpath's late-2024 bankruptcy and the contract turnover that followed left counties scrambling for medical vendors. Deaths-in-custody litigation keeps rising. Opioid-settlement dollars are flowing to county jails for medication for opioid use disorder. A growing number of state Medicaid reentry waivers require medication continuity at release. Independents need any revenue line that does not depend on PBM reimbursement.
revenue_model: County per-diem or monthly retainer (roughly $1,500-6,000 a month per small jail, to be validated by state). The pharmacy pays a 10-15% platform fee plus $300-600 a month for the software. Additional revenue from risk-pool partnership programs and discharge-supply services.
non_obvious_insight: Rural jail medication is not a healthcare problem, it is a liability problem the sheriff cannot outsource to a national vendor that ships in five days. The real buyer is the county risk pool and insurer, and the independent pharmacist next door is the only entity that can deliver in thirty minutes. Small contracts often fall below county bid thresholds, and the sheriff already knows the pharmacist by first name.
first_30_days: The pharmacist calls the sheriff in their own county and offers a 60-day pilot at cost. Audit the jail's med room and write a one-page deficiency list. Propose eMAR plus packaging. Check the state pharmacy board's rules for institutional or correctional pharmacy licensure. Pitch the results to the state sheriffs' association and the county risk pool, and recruit two neighboring independents to copy the model.

title: AI Chat-History Exposure Assessments for Breach Counsel
one_liner: When infostealers grab employees' AI sessions, tell breach counsel what the attacker could actually have read and whether notification is triggered.
customer: Incident-response boutiques, privacy and breach law firms, cyber-insurer panel vendors, and enterprise DPOs. Priced per incident.
problem: Infostealer logs exposed AI sessions tied to 80,000+ corporate domains, and 358 of 482 large companies analyzed had stolen ChatGPT/OpenAI sessions. A stolen session is a searchable archive of contracts, source code, and personal data, and it bypasses MFA. IR tooling was built for mailboxes and file shares, so nobody can say whether an AI-history breach triggers legal notification.
solution: Ingest infostealer-feed hits mapped to employee AI accounts. Combine them with the customer's enterprise export or compliance-API data to classify the sampled chats after the theft window by data class (PII, PHI, credentials, deal information, source code). Deliver a notification-decision memo, an affected-person list, remediation steps (session revocation, key rotation), and an insurer-ready timeline.
why_now: The 2026 infostealer data shows stolen AI sessions at scale. Enterprise AI adoption now puts sensitive work in chat, and insurers are adding AI exclusions, so they want scoping evidence before paying.
revenue_model: $5-25K per incident, with $1-2K per month monitoring retainers and channel referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: The breach is not the stolen cookie but the content behind it, and notification law turns on data, not credentials. No tool in the IR stack handles AI transcripts, so a small team can own the category before platform vendors bother.
first_30_days: Sign 3 IR boutiques as channel partners. Build a classification pipeline over enterprise chat exports. Run the first paid assessments at a $7.5K flat fee using hits from commercial infostealer-intel feeds.

title: Brewery Tank-Time for Fermentation Startups
one_liner: Rent the empty fermenters of struggling craft breweries to early-stage fermentation companies that cannot get pilot-scale capacity, with standard SOPs and insurance.
customer: Buyers: seed-to-Series-A companies making probiotics and postbiotics, lactic-acid-bacteria and yeast-based ingredients, cultured foods, kombucha-adjacent drinks and biocontrol products that need 1 to 30 kL runs. Sellers: craft breweries, cideries and distilleries with idle tanks.
problem: Pilot-scale food-grade fermentation capacity is scarce and expensive for startups. Meanwhile the Brewers Association says breweries used only about 55% of capacity in 2024, there were 481 closures against 300 openings in 2025, and US craft breweries fell to 9,344 by June 2026. Neither side knows how to contract safely, and food-safety, TTB and insurance issues block informal deals.
solution: A marketplace with a standardized brewery-as-CDMO package: BSL-1 organism screening, cleaning and changeover SOPs, food-facility registration checks, TTB premises guidance, a template contract and insurer-backed coverage. A rentable clip-on aeration and dissolved-oxygen kit extends tanks to low-aeration aerobic processes. Startups book tank-days and downstream time (centrifuge, filtration, cold room).
why_now: Craft brewing is in a third year of decline, with real estate and tank capacity stranded. Startup funding is tight, so cheap pilot capacity matters. Sensors and remote fermentation monitoring make third-party oversight feasible.
revenue_model: Startups pay $300 to $900 per tank-day; the brewery keeps about 80%, the platform takes 15% to 20%. Fees for SOP set-up, kit rental and insurance referral.
non_obvious_insight: Tanks are not the scarce input; validated protocols and biosafety trust are. Most brewery fermenters are unstirred and anaerobic, so the honest wedge is anaerobic and low-aeration products, with an aeration retrofit unlocking more later. A platform that standardizes the SOP and contract becomes the default channel.
first_30_days: Recruit 8 breweries within a few hours of Boston, the Bay Area or Denver that have idle 10-to-30-barrel fermenters. Work with a food-safety consultant to write a one-organism SOP. Approach 25 fermentation startups and run 3 paid pilot batches at $2k to $5k each.

title: Peak-Window Uptime Plans for Fishing Boats
one_liner: A seasonal membership that pre-stages each boat's likely failure parts and rebuilt swap components in the harbor, provides RSW and hydraulic mechanics on call, and later adds a paid lost-peak-days cover.
customer: Bristol Bay and Prince William Sound drift and set net owners, plus seiners, who pay $2,000-4,000 per boat per season. A fleet of a few hundred boats is a $1M-plus business. Later an insurance partner underwrites the lost-time cover.
problem: Most of a boat's year is earned in about 10-14 days. With 2026's $1.72/lb, a busy boat can earn $5-15K a day at peak. Hull and machinery insurance pays for repair, never for the lost fishing days. A raw-water impeller, hydraulic hose, reel motor, fuel filter or failed RSW system takes a boat out for three days because the part is on a barge or a bush flight that's booked solid. The whole fleet breaks the same dozen components in the same ten days.
solution: Catalog the top 15-20 failure modes by engine and hydraulic setup. Stage member-funded kits in secure containers at Naknek, Dillingham, Egegik and similar harbors by June 1. Hold a rotating pool of rebuilt swap cores (injection pumps, hydraulic pumps, reel motors). Contract freelance diesel, hydraulic and RSW mechanics on retainer for guaranteed response times. Members can order from the grounds by satellite text. Phase two: verified downtime (AIS, dock check-in, mechanic log) triggers a fixed per-day payment during declared peak windows through an MGA partner.
why_now: The 2026 price rebound made every fishing day worth much more than in 2025. The fleet is aging. RSW is now paid for (about $0.15/lb bonus at some processors), yet the regional development association is funding apprentices because there aren't enough RSW technicians. Starlink lets skippers order parts and report faults from the fishing grounds.
revenue_model: Membership fees of $2-4K per boat per season, parts and swap-core margin, mechanic call-out fees, and a later per-day parametric lost-time premium shared with the underwriter.
non_obvious_insight: Downtime costs are about timing, not repair. The scarce resource at peak is the right part on the right beach within hours, and nobody sells that. It works as pooled inventory: because the fleet fails predictably, a small stockpile insures hundreds of boats. Insurance pooling for parts is cheaper and faster to launch than insurance pooling for money.
first_30_days: Interview 30 skippers and mechanics at the November Pacific Marine Expo in Seattle and by phone with Naknek and Dillingham crews. Build the failure-mode parts list by engine and hydraulic setup. Pre-sell 40 memberships with $500 deposits by February. Line up two freelance mechanics and one RSW tech. Rent a container in one harbor and stage the first 40 boats' kits by June 1.

title: Medicaid Work-Rule Retention for Hospitals and Plans
one_liner: A text-first service that proves work hours and exemptions on behalf of Medicaid members, paid per retained member by the hospitals and health plans that would otherwise lose them.
customer: Safety-net hospitals, FQHC networks and Medicaid managed-care plans in expansion states. They pay roughly $4-12 per retained member per month or a fee per successful report.
problem: Under the 2025 budget law (OBBBA), expansion adults aged 19-64 must document about 80 hours a month of work, school or volunteering, or prove an exemption, with more frequent renewals. Deadlines start no later than January 1, 2027, with limited state extensions. Arkansas in 2018 showed that people mostly lost coverage from reporting failures, not from ineligibility. Members lose coverage over paperwork. Hospitals and plans then lose revenue and absorb uncompensated care.
solution: A retention layer that sits on the member side. It works over SMS and WhatsApp in multiple languages. It connects to the member's payroll, gig-platform earnings, school enrollment or caregiver records to auto-assemble monthly proof. It screens for the many exemptions (medically frail, parents of young children, substance-use treatment, recent release) and generates provider attestation letters from the clinic's own visit. It submits in each state's format, using portal automation and mail-in where needed. It nags before deadlines. A dashboard shows the plan or hospital which members are at risk before the coverage cliff. The same engine later covers SNAP work rules.
why_now: The law was signed in July 2025, and federal guidance and state build-outs are happening now for the 2027 start. Some states, such as Georgia with Pathways, already run work-reporting programs. The large incumbents (state-agency contractors) build for the state side, not for retention on the member side. Hospital CFOs are modeling large expansion-population losses this budget cycle. LLM agents plus computer-use can drive dozens of clunky state portals that never had APIs. Gig and payroll data connections make proof of hours automatic.
revenue_model: Per-member-per-month retention fee, or per-successful-report fee, paid by hospitals, FQHCs and plans. Later, state contracts and a SNAP work-requirement product on the same infrastructure.
non_obvious_insight: The payer is neither the patient nor the state. It is whoever loses revenue when a member drops. The failure is documentation friction, not eligibility. The cheapest evidence source is the member's own gig or payroll account plus the clinic visit itself, which can collect exemption proof for free.
first_30_days: Choose one state with an early or waiver-driven start and a large FQHC association. Meet revenue-cycle and financial-counseling leads at 5 FQHCs and hospitals. Publish a free state-by-state 'Am I exempt? Do my hours count?' checker to generate leads. Run a manual SMS concierge pilot with 200 members using a spreadsheet and volunteers, and measure on-time reporting rate. Convert the best result into a signed letter of intent for a per-retained-member fee.

title: Independent Auditor of Real Agent-Commerce Volume
one_liner: A neutral measurement firm that separates real agent payments from wash trading and testing, then sells diligence to investors and behavioral AML monitoring to the trust banks that carry the flows.
customer: Investors and acquirers diligencing agent-payment startups, protocol foundations and ecosystem funds that allocate grants on volume, OCC-chartered trust banks, stablecoin issuers and MSBs onboarding agent-wallet fintechs, and card networks and acquirers.
problem: Bloomberg found that about $24M of on-chain agent commerce shrinks to about $1.6M once self-trading wallets are removed, and Base logged about 97M protocol transactions with no one able to say how many were live. Meanwhile Tempo raised $500M and every network is announcing agent rails. KYC at onboarding does not fit wallets that act autonomously, and continuous behavioral KYC is the flagged gap.
solution: Cluster wallets, detect self-dealing, and classify each flow as test, wash or real economic activity (unique counterparties, fiat off-ramps, merchant tie-outs) across x402, MPP and AP2 settlement. Publish a free index, sell diligence reports, and offer an agent-tuned monitoring API that scores velocity, counterparty concentration and sanctions-adjacent exposure for BSA/AML programs.
why_now: x402 moved to the Linux Foundation in April 2026 and MPP is live. The Fed proposed GENIUS Act issuer rules on 2026-09-24, and OCC trust charters are being handed out (Circle on 2026-07-10, Coinbase in April, Bridge conditionally). A Senate report alleging about $2B of Iran-linked Tether flows raises the cost of weak compliance.
revenue_model: Diligence engagements at $15-60k each, monitoring subscriptions at $5-30k per month per bank or issuer, and data licensing to funds and networks.
non_obvious_insight: In a hype market the scarce good is credible measurement, and a firm with no token or protocol stake is the only party everyone can trust. The clustering work that debunks the volume numbers is the same compliance product regulated banks will have to buy, and it needs both on-chain forensics and agent-protocol fluency.
first_30_days: Two on-chain analysts build the wash filter on public data (Dune or Flipside), publish 'Real vs Reported Agent Commerce' with an open methodology, and pitch it to 15 funds and 3 foundations. Charge for the first bespoke diligence report within the month, and let the free index drive inbound.

title: Wearable-Triggered Spending Guardrails for Sports Bettors
one_liner: A debit card and betting-budget wallet that tightens gambling, day-trading and BNPL limits automatically when the wearer's sleep, heart-rate variability and late-night pattern predict impulsive decisions, with an optional spouse or sponsor as co-guardian.
customer: US adults who bet legally on sports or prediction markets and want limits: self-referred users, partners and recovery groups first. Credit unions and employer assistance programs are the B2B2C channel. The price is $6-9 a month.
problem: Roughly 40 states have legal sports betting and sports prediction contracts have spread. Household credit stress is at record levels, with delinquencies at highs and deposits often funded by cards or BNPL. Existing blocks are all-or-nothing, and willpower fails at 2 a.m. after a losing streak. A wearable knows when the user is depleted, but the bank has never seen that signal.
solution: An issued card and ledger, built on a card-issuing platform, that funds a weekly betting wallet. The user pre-commits the rules when calm. If sleep drops below a set threshold, HRV falls against baseline, or two late-night losses stack up, the wallet enters a 24-hour cooldown, cuts the daily cap, or asks a partner to approve top-ups. Wearable sync is opt-in via Oura, Whoop, Garmin or Apple Health. Only a one-bit cooldown flag leaves the phone.
why_now: Legal betting and prediction-market sports contracts scaled through 2025-26. Brazil banned online betting and announced debt relief on Sept 25, 2026, showing the politics have turned. The CFPB open-banking rule is stayed and unstable, so a business built on card-level controls avoids dependence on aggregator data. Wearables are now mainstream, with Whoop raising $575M this year.
revenue_model: $7 a month subscription plus interchange share. Credit unions and neobanks license it for $1-2 per member per month. State problem-gambling councils pay for evidence-based tools. Anything sold to sportsbooks is optional and kept separate to avoid conflicts.
non_obvious_insight: Financial products treat every hour as equal, but behavior is not. The best predictor of a regretted transaction is the user's physiological state at 1 a.m., which the user's own wearable measures and the bank never sees. Sell control, not surveillance: the user writes the rules in advance and a bank never sees raw health data.
first_30_days: Ship a no-card MVP: an SMS and Slack bot that uses the Oura or Whoop API to send cooldown alerts, plus a partner-approval flow. Recruit 50 users from recovering-bettor communities. Measure whether cooldowns cut after-midnight deposits. Then pilot with one credit union that already offers gambling merchant-category blocks, and price at $7 a month.

title: Lend Against Battery Earnings for Vet Bills
one_liner: A wallet that routes VPP and demand-response payouts into a dedicated pet-care fund, then advances emergency vet money against the battery's telemetry-verified future earnings.
customer: Home-battery owners in VPPs (repayment via payout offset). Partners who pay are VPP aggregators and retail energy providers (retention) and pet insurers (customer acquisition).
problem: Vet bills are lumpy and emotional: 85% of vet professionals say clients decline care at estimates of $1,000 or less, and 13% of euthanasias are attributed to inability to pay. Only about 5% of US dogs and cats are insured, while premiums rose 19.7% against 9% growth in insured animals, which invites churn. High-APR deferred-interest cards are the fallback. Meanwhile VPP payouts are small, abstract and easily ignored, even though dispatch is real (580 MW from 140,000 California batteries on September 9, 2026).
solution: Owners assign payouts to a Pet Reserve that auto-pays insurance premiums and pre-funds vet bills at partner clinics. Once the balance builds, they can draw an advance repaid from future dispatch payments, underwritten on battery telemetry and contracted programs. Start with credits and premium payments only, and add advances through a bank or lender partner once the data is proven.
why_now: VPPs are now large enough to have contracted, metered payout streams (Base Power raised $1B with a 500+ MWh fleet; Sunrun/Tesla dispatch). Pet insurance repricing is pushing owners to look for offsets, and no aggregator owns a consumer-finance layer.
revenue_model: Referral bounty from pet insurers ($50-150 per policy), retention/SaaS fee from aggregators or retailers, and interest or fee spread on repayable advances via a lending partner.
non_obvious_insight: A battery in a VPP is a telemetry-verified income stream, and it is collateralizable. Converting abstract kWh payouts into 'vet visits' also changes how much owners value flexibility, and the pet emergency is the highest-emotion, lowest-friction use of the credit.
first_30_days: Recruit one small VPP operator or retail energy provider (not Tesla) and 300-500 pet-owning households through battery-owner communities. Launch payout-to-Pet-Fund with premium auto-pay and a referral deal with one insurer. Measure opt-in, retention and how many households use the balance for vet bills. Hold advances until a lending partner and legal review are in place.

title: Betting Profit-and-Loss Statements for Credit Unions
one_liner: Turn a member's bank ACH data into an 'investment-style' betting P&L (what they recovered per dollar deposited) and optional spending guardrails, licensed per member to credit unions and neobanks.
customer: Community banks, credit unions with young or college-town memberships, and neobanks, paying $0.25-0.60 per member per month. A free consumer version targets Gen Z bettors and their worried parents or partners.
problem: Online betting and prediction-market use is surging among the young. In June-July 2026 first-time users were about 3x January levels. Gen Z and Millennials were 88% of activity (Gen Z 48%). Bettors recovered under 75 cents per dollar sent to platforms. 23% of sports bettors bet daily and 34% weekly. Households that bet had a median deposit balance of only 59% of non-bettors'. Most of these users do not think of themselves as gamblers: 20% of respondents call sports betting a type of investment, Gen Z is about twice as likely to, and buying prediction-market event contracts is more likely to be called an investment than sports betting is.
solution: A detector that classifies ACH and card flows to sportsbooks, sweepstakes casinos and event-contract exchanges, using a maintained list of originator and descriptor names. It produces a plain 'Your realized return: -27%' statement in the vocabulary bettors already use (returns, cost basis), with a monthly summary and opt-in deposit caps or a cooling-off freeze. A parent, partner or co-guardian mode makes it useful for Gen Z members who live at home. The consumer version is a free upload-your-statement tool that generates a shareable 'what's your recovery ratio' card, which doubles as the top of the funnel for credit-union licenses.
why_now: Prediction markets went mainstream in 2026 and the FIFA World Cup drove the June-July spike. Football season, which overlaps other major leagues, starts a new peak now, and first-time users grew 22% YoY in the 2025 football season. Regulators and financial institutions are still working out how to treat event contracts. Under BofA's own framing they sit in a gray zone between entertainment and investing.
revenue_model: B2B: $2-5K/month pilot fees, then $0.25-0.60 per member per month. B2C: free P&L tool, $4.99/month for caps and alerts, and paid family co-guardian seats. Possible later add-on: aggregate, anonymized risk analytics for lenders.
non_obvious_insight: Self-serve gambling blocks fail because bettors do not classify themselves as gamblers, so a harm-reduction message framed as 'gambling addiction' gets ignored, while a return-on-investment statement speaks their mental model. BofA identified betting activity purely from ACH flows, which shows any bank can build the same detection. Working hypothesis, not verified because my search budget ran out: card merchant-category-code blocks used by many banks probably miss ACH-funded prediction-market deposits. Validate with two or three credit-union risk teams before building. Evidence: https://institute.bankofamerica.com/economic-insights/online-betting-platforms.html and its full PDF https://institute.bankofamerica.com/content/dam/economic-insights/online-betting-platforms.pdf (3x first-timers, recovery under 75 cents, 88% Gen Z plus Millennials, 20% see betting as investing, 59% median balance).
first_30_days: Week 1: compile a list of ACH originator and descriptor names for major sportsbooks, sweepstakes casinos and event-contract exchanges, and ship a client-side upload-a-CSV P&L calculator with a shareable result card. Week 2: seed it in Gen Z finance and sports-betting subreddits and Discords to collect real recovery-ratio numbers. Week 3: cold-email 30 credit unions near universities and military bases (member-financial-wellness and CUSO contacts) with the anonymized ratio data. Week 4: sign one or two paid pilots at $2-5K/month. Legal review of state gambling-related messaging rules is required before launch.

title: Dispute Escrow for Agent Payments on Pix/UPI
one_liner: A neutral hold-and-evidence layer that gives agent-initiated Pix and UPI payments the dispute protection cards have and push rails never did.
customer: Brazilian WhatsApp-commerce, bill-pay and shopping-agent startups and their sponsoring payment institutions, plus Indian UPI apps building agentic checkout. Marketplaces and merchants who want to accept agent buyers are the second payer.
problem: Pix, UPI and M-Pesa are push rails: instantly final, with no chargeback culture. When an agent buys the wrong SKU, gets prompt-injected, or loops, the money is simply gone. Visa and Mastercard still have no binding agent-chargeback rule, and the ledger shows only amount, time and merchant, with no record of why the agent paid. Merchants cannot tell a legitimate agent buyer from an abusive one, and PSPs cannot price the risk.
solution: An API that wraps agent-initiated push payments in a short programmable hold (2-24h) through a licensed partner PSP's escrow or split-payment accounts, or through UPI block-and-debit mandates. Each payment carries a signed 'decision receipt': the user's mandate, a hash of the agent's tool-call trace, price-check evidence and model version. A small human adjudication desk releases or refunds by published rules. PSPs, merchants and insurers all accept the receipt as evidence. The SDK is free; money movement and adjudication are the paid layer.
why_now: Agent rails (AP2 mandates, Mastercard Verifiable Intent, MPP, x402, ACP/UCP) all solve authorization but none define fault or evidence for push rails. India ends zero-MDR UPI for large P2M payments on Oct 15, and a rail that starts charging merchants acquires card-like dispute expectations. Insurers are adding AI exclusions, so they need telemetry to price anything. The Ninth Circuit's 'the agent is the user' ruling pushes liability toward users and their intermediaries.
revenue_model: 0.2-0.4% of held volume, $0.02-0.05 per receipt at scale, and dispute-handling fees paid by whichever side loses. Later, an evidence-pack license to PSPs and insurers underwriting agent risk.
non_obvious_insight: In emerging markets most digital volume rides rails with no chargeback system, so agent error is an unhedged first-class risk there. Whoever holds the neutral, tamper-evident record of why an agent paid becomes the arbiter, and eventually the underwriter, for every party. The cards networks are structurally slow to solve this for rails they do not run.
first_30_days: Publish an open-source decision-receipt SDK for agents that pay via Pix or UPI. Recruit 10 small agent builders (WhatsApp bill-pay and shopping bots) on developer communities. Sign one licensed PSP for escrow sandbox accounts. Hand-adjudicate the first 100 disputes yourselves to learn the fault taxonomy, then price the hold as a paid tier.

title: Escrow and Tax Rails for Agent-Hired Humans
one_liner: The compliance and payment layer that lets software agents legally hire humans for judgment and real-world tasks: owner KYC, task-legality screening, escrow, worker classification and tax forms.
customer: Agent-framework developers and companies whose agents need on-call humans (verification, phone calls, notarisation, in-person checks), plus the workers doing the tasks. Take rate is 8-12%.
problem: Agent-to-human marketplaces are appearing (47jobs, Hirenewtalent.ai in the brief, and viral 'rent a human' sites in early 2026), but nobody is the clear payor, employer or liable party. Who issues 1099s, who is responsible if an agent sends someone to do something illegal or never pays, and how do workers avoid scams?
solution: An API plus MCP tool ('ask_human'): agents post tasks against funded escrow tied to a KYC'd human or company principal. A legality and safety classifier rejects risky tasks. Automatic tax forms and classification, dispute arbitration and two-sided reputation follow, with optional injury insurance for physical tasks.
why_now: Agent frameworks and MCP matured in 2025, agent-payment standards and stablecoin rails are being rolled out, and agent-run marketplaces are going viral. Regulators will demand a principal of record after the first scandal.
revenue_model: 8-12% take rate on tasks plus an insurance margin for physical work.
non_obvious_insight: The marketplace is cheap to clone. The moat is the principal-of-record and liability layer, which is what regulators and enterprise buyers will eventually require, so building the compliant rails first wins the boring middle.
first_30_days: Ship a minimal escrow API and MCP tool with 200 vetted workers in one niche (phone verification calls, document notarisation, local checks in 3 cities). Onboard 10 agent builders through Discord and HN and complete the first 500 paid tasks.

title: Percentage-Rent Rails for Small Retail Strips
one_liner: Sales-linked leases with rent automatically swept from the tenant's POS, so independent landlords can fill dark restaurant and shop spaces and tenants stop dying under fixed rent.
customer: Owner-operator landlords of neighborhood retail strips and mixed-use buildings with vacancy, and independent restaurants and retailers seeking space. Platform revenue comes from landlords and processed rent.
problem: Higher rates and a squeezed consumer are closing independents. Landlords face 6-12 months of vacancy and costly tenant improvements. Percentage-rent leases align risk, but small landlords do not trust tenants' sales reports, so the structure has been confined to big malls.
solution: A standard 'base plus percent' lease template (a lower base of about 50-60% of market plus 5-8% of gross sales above a breakpoint). Rent is computed and swept automatically from Toast, Square or Clover data with tenant consent, and the landlord sees a live dashboard. Add leasing and brokerage, and a lender-facing cash-flow report so landlords can refinance on more predictable income.
why_now: Refinancing at higher rates pushes landlords to prefer occupied space. Rates just rose again and the consumer is K-shaped. POS APIs and embedded payments now make sales reporting verifiable and rent collection automatic for small operators.
revenue_model: 1-2% of rent flow processed, a leasing commission on placements, and a lender-reporting subscription. Optional financing spread for landlords.
non_obvious_insight: Percentage rent died in small retail because of an information problem, not an economics problem, and POS data solves the information problem. Because landlord income scales with tenant sales, the system flips the landlord from adversary to partner and wins in booms as well as downturns.
first_30_days: Recruit three landlords with vacant restaurant or retail spaces in one metro. Have a lawyer draft the lease template. Build Toast and Square OAuth plus ACH sweeps with existing tools. Sign two tenants on sales-linked leases and use their first rent runs as proof.

title: Hidden Satellite Tags Against Fictitious Pickups
one_liner: A cargo custody kit that pairs a verified-carrier check at pickup with several disposable Bluetooth-to-satellite tags hidden in each load, giving brokers and insurers evidence of where freight went when it was stolen.
customer: Mid-size freight brokers (20-200 staff) and 3PLs moving theft-prone loads (electronics, pharma, beverages, copper) on US and cross-border lanes, and inland-marine cargo insurers or MGAs that have raised deductibles on theft. Start with brokers hit by fictitious pickups.
problem: Thieves impersonate legitimate carriers and dispatchers (increasingly with cloned voices), pick up loads and vanish. The one expensive GPS tracker per trailer is found and jammed, cell-based devices fail in remote drop points, and the broker learns hours later. Paperwork chains are spoofable, and insurers cannot prove the exact custody break.
solution: (1) An identity gate at pickup that partners with existing carrier-verification vendors (MC/DOT match, live driver ID, verified call-back). (2) Three to five disposable $5-12 Bluetooth-to-satellite tags bound to the bill of lading at pickup and hidden in cartons. (3) An evidence timeline of last-seen sightings from orbit, including where there is no cell coverage, compared against the declared route. (4) Police-ready location packets and an insurer-accepted custody report that earns premium credits.
why_now: Bluetooth-to-satellite just crossed into serious capital: Hubble Network raised a $200M Series C at a $1.6B valuation on 28 Sept 2026, with 6 satellites up and a next generation in 2027 aiming at much lower-power detection. Cheaper launch is collapsing per-tag and per-message costs. Voice-clone impersonation and business email compromise ($3.05B in US losses) make carrier identity fraud easier.
revenue_model: $12-25 per protected load with volume tiers, an insurer revenue share on premium credits, and annual platform fees for brokers with more than 5,000 loads.
non_obvious_insight: Trackers fail because thieves can find and defeat the single expensive device. When a tag costs $6 and needs no phone network, a broker can hide many of them, and abundance beats stealth. Current sat-BLE revisit times are hours, so the product is priced as last-seen evidence and recovery, not live tracking. The true buyer is often the insurer, who values proof of the custody-break moment.
first_30_days: Buy 500 tags through the vendor developer program. Recruit 3 brokers via freight-intermediary association networks. Tag every load on their two highest-theft lanes at cost for 30 days and log coverage and gaps. Bring the results to two cargo MGAs and negotiate a premium-credit pilot.

title: Drug Safety Radar for Pet Medicines
one_liner: A real-world evidence network that reads clinic notes and insurance claims to spot adverse events for newly launched pet drugs and biologics, sold to manufacturers as pharmacovigilance.
customer: Animal-health manufacturers' safety and medical-affairs teams and biotechs launching first-in-class pet therapeutics; later regulators' contractors and insurers.
problem: Adverse-event reporting in vet medicine is voluntary and sparse, and clinics rarely file forms. New launches are arriving on conditional approvals and emergency authorizations, and the post-market evidence burden is growing.
solution: Consent-based feeds from ambient-scribe notes, PIMS and insurer claims. LLMs extract exposures and events, auto-draft FDA-format adverse-event reports in one click for clinics, and run signal detection with matched comparison cohorts. First product: a fixed-fee retrospective signal report for one drug class using one insurer's de-identified claims plus 20-50 clinics.
why_now: FDA has issued 15 emergency authorizations and 3 conditional approvals for screwworm drugs as of 2026-09-03, and Loyal's LOY-002 has cleared two of three technical sections with launch possible before year-end. Ambient scribes turn notes into structured text, and IDEXX/CoVet suggests data will get walled off by incumbents.
revenue_model: $50-250K per drug program per year, per-report fees, and data licensing.
non_obvious_insight: When launches lean on conditional approvals and emergency authorizations, evidence generation becomes a cost manufacturers must pay, not a nice-to-have. The winning data source is neutral: insurers plus clinics through scribes, not the PIMS vendors who will gate access.
first_30_days: Contact safety and medical-affairs leads at 5 mid-size animal-health companies. Propose a $40K retrospective signal study on a public safety question with an insurer data partner. Release a free one-click adverse-event drafting tool to 20 clinics to seed data.

title: Origin Assay: Forensic Testing of Metal Melt Origin
one_liner: A lab test that says where steel or aluminum was actually melted, so US-melt claims stop resting on paperwork alone.
customer: Importers and fabricators claiming the 10% US-melt rate, steel service centers selling premium 'US-melt' stock, customs counsel and insurers defending CBP audits, and buyers with domestic-metal requirements.
problem: Section 232 rates now depend on melt or smelt origin: 10% with US-melted metal against 25-50%. The certificate is worth thousands of dollars per ton, mill test reports can be relabeled or forged, and CBP is prioritizing origin verification and AD/CVD evasion. No independent test exists.
solution: Build a reference library by buying coupons from about 100 mills worldwide. Measure trace-element, inclusion and slag chemistry, and isotopic signatures (LIBS, ICP-MS, SEM-EDS). Train a classifier to give origin probability. First product is a mail-in Origin Assay with a confidence-scored report and sampling protocol built for audits. Handheld screening is a later roadmap. Classifier accuracy is the central risk, so start with one narrow discrimination, such as US EAF versus Chinese plate for one grade.
why_now: The 2026 tiers turn a chemistry fact into a financial asset. Cheaper mass spectrometry and machine learning make library-based classification plausible, and academic provenance work exists but no commercial library does (verify).
revenue_model: $300-900 per sample. $25-100k annual audit programs for service centers. Insurer verification programs. Later, handheld subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Duty policy turned melt origin into money, and paper certificates invite cheating, so the arbitrage is proof. Scrap-based EAF steel carries a fingerprint of tramp elements and alloy history that makes origin partly knowable.
first_30_days: Interview three service centers and three customs counsel. Buy or borrow about 40 heats of known origin (A36 and 304). Use a university ICP-MS lab to test discriminating power on two grades. Sell a $5k pilot verification of 10 suspicious heats.

title: Sleep-Apnea-to-GLP-1 Pathway for DME Suppliers
one_liner: A co-management service that lets sleep labs and CPAP suppliers prescribe, retest and retain patients as they lose weight.
customer: Independent sleep centers, home-sleep-test companies and DME suppliers whose profit engine is CPAP resupply.
problem: Zepbound was approved for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity on Dec 20, 2024, and Part D can cover it for OSA. As weight falls, patients drop CPAP without a retest or re-titration, and the DME loses resupply revenue and the patient. Sleep clinics have no pathway for prescribing or co-managing a drug.
solution: Baseline and 3/6/12-month home sleep tests, benefits verification and prior authorization for Zepbound-for-OSA, a nutrition and muscle plan, auto-CPAP pressure re-titration from device data, and a 'retest before you quit CPAP' protocol. DMEs keep the supply relationship where still needed.
why_now: The OSA indication now has Medicare and commercial coverage routes, and cash pricing is falling, so patient demand is arriving at sleep clinics without a pathway. DMEs see the threat and hold the patient data (CPAP usage) needed to co-manage.
revenue_model: $15-30 per patient per month to the DME or sleep center, or a share of retained resupply, plus per-test fees.
non_obvious_insight: The DME supplier looks like the loser but is the natural gatekeeper: it has adherence data, patient trust and a recurring billing relationship, and it will pay to convert lost resupply into a managed weight-and-airway program.
first_30_days: Approach 5 regional DMEs or sleep centers. Pilot on 100 CPAP patients with BMI of 30 or more and AHI of 15 or more. Measure PA success, retest rate and retained resupply.
